turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Come through, have a seat. We're running a bit late, I'm afraid.
[SEG0002] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): We got lost in the car park anyway. He's been in a mood since he woke.
[SEG0003] person_3 (PATIENT): I'm tired. Not a mood. Can we start.
[SEG0004] person_1 (DOCTOR): What's brought you in today?
[SEG0005] person_3 (PATIENT): Woke up and the left side of my face has dropped.
[SEG0006] person_3 (PATIENT): I can't shut the left eye. Can't whistle either, I had a go.
[SEG0007] person_1 (DOCTOR): Was it like that the second you woke?
[SEG0008] person_3 (PATIENT): Yeah. Toothpaste and water just fell out the left side of my mouth.
[SEG0009] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any weakness in the arm, or the leg?
[SEG0010] person_3 (PATIENT): No. Took the bin out fine. Arms are normal.
[SEG0011] person_1 (DOCTOR): Speech, any slurring, or trouble finding words?
[SEG0012] person_3 (PATIENT): No. Talking's fine. I'm just, uh, irritable.
[SEG0013] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any dizziness?
[SEG0014] person_3 (PATIENT): Not really.
[SEG0015] person_1 (DOCTOR): And is the face painful?
[SEG0016] person_3 (PATIENT): Not painful. Ear was sore yesterday, behind the left one. That's gone.
[SEG0017] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He grumbled about the ear last night, in the middle of that baking programme. I said it was the draught.
[SEG0018] person_3 (PATIENT): Wasn't a draught. It ached. It's stopped now.
[SEG0019] person_1 (DOCTOR): Headache today? Sickness?
[SEG0020] person_3 (PATIENT): No headache. Not that either. I haven't been sick.
[SEG0021] person_1 (DOCTOR): Ever had a droop like this before?
[SEG0022] person_3 (PATIENT): Never.
[SEG0023] person_1 (DOCTOR): Long-term problems I should know about?
[SEG0024] person_3 (PATIENT): Asthma. Err, for years.
[SEG0025] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): They did his cholesterol at the surgery last year too. Said it was borderline. He left it.
[SEG0026] person_1 (DOCTOR): Mm. So they called it borderline, and there's no number in front of me. I won't chase a result I can't see. Which inhalers?
[SEG0027] person_3 (PATIENT): Salbutamol, two puffs when I need it. And, uh, beclomethosone, two puffs morning and night.
[SEG0028] person_1 (DOCTOR): Beclometasone. Any allergies?
[SEG0029] person_3 (PATIENT): No. Never.
[SEG0030] person_1 (DOCTOR): Do you smoke at all?
[SEG0031] person_3 (PATIENT): Not really. Well, I packed it in, years ago.
[SEG0032] person_1 (DOCTOR): Alcohol?
[SEG0033] person_3 (PATIENT): A couple of beers at the weekend. Can we get to the point.
[SEG0034] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any problems with the waterworks?
[SEG0035] person_3 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0036] person_1 (DOCTOR): Sudden droop, my plan would be A&E today for a CT head, to make sure this isn't a stroke.
[SEG0037] person_3 (PATIENT): I am not going to A&E. Arm's fine. I already said.
[SEG0038] person_1 (DOCTOR): Of. Fair enough. Let me examine you first. Lift the eyebrows.
[SEG0039] person_1 (DOCTOR): Left forehead doesn't move. Close the eyes tight. The left stays open a gap, and the left corner of the mouth doesn't lift when you smile.
[SEG0040] person_3 (PATIENT): I know how it looks. Just get on with it.
[SEG0041] person_1 (DOCTOR): Grip is equal both sides. Speech has stayed clear. Blood pressure is 136 over 84, pulse 78.
[SEG0042] person_1 (DOCTOR): The asthma wheeze, is that playing up?
[SEG0043] person_3 (PATIENT): No... well, sometimes, if I leg it for the bus.
[SEG0044] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Wheezes on the hill by the co-op. Has for ages, not every day.
[SEG0045] person_1 (DOCTOR): Sometimes when you hurry, then. Not all the time. Short of breath sitting in that chair?
[SEG0046] person_3 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0047] person_1 (DOCTOR): Right. That examination changes my plan. Forehead involved, no arm weakness, speech intact, so no A&E and no scan.
[SEG0048] person_1 (DOCTOR): Working impression is a left Bell's palsy. Provisional, I haven't proved it on a picture.
[SEG0049] person_3 (PATIENT): Call it what you like. The eye keeps watering and I'm shattered.

[SEG0050] person_1 (DOCTOR): Prednisolone 50 mg once a day by mouth for 10 days, start today, take it with food. For the eye, artificial tears from the chemist in the daytime, and tape the left eye shut at night.

[SEG0051] person_1 (DOCTOR): If the eye goes red, the vision blurs, or an arm goes weak, get seen the same day. Otherwise I'll see you back in one week. Keep the salbutamol and the beclometasone as they are. Nothing for that borderline cholesterol.

[SEG0052] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'll say it back. Face dropped on waking, can't close the eye or whistle, the eye's watering, ear ached yesterday then settled, face not painful, no arm weakness, speech alright, not really dizzy, no headache, not been sick, never happened before. Asthma for years, wheeze only sometimes if you rush. Cholesterol was called borderline last year, no figure. Steroid, eye care, back in a week. Not the scan.

spec.situation: Person woke with one side of the face drooping, cannot close the eye, cannot whistle; no arm weakness, no speech problem, ear pain a day before; doctor examines and starts steroids, eye care explained.

traps.happens: The patient denies some symptoms (said as 'no', 'not really', 'never'), has a chronic condition named earlier (for example asthma or hypertension) and later the doctor asks about another symptom of it, and one answer is a double negative or a correction ('not that either', 'no... well, sometimes').
traps.label_rule: Denials go in negative_findings with the exact thing denied, never in symptoms. NEVER write a negative about a condition the patient has said they have. A corrected answer keeps only the final version. A negative is never a symptom, and 'not painful' is the finding 'pain' absent, not a symptom called 'painless'.

features: doctor_changes_mind: the doctor says one plan, then changes it after new information; the label holds the final plan.
test_result_recalled: the patient reports an old test or result ('they said it was borderline'); recorded as reported history/investigation only as far as said, not as a confirmed value.

bad.reason: Patient said 'Not really,' not a clear absence of dizziness.

omissions.text: Initial plan was A&E the same day for a CT head to make sure this was not a stroke, but the patient refused to go to A&E; after examination the doctor changed plan to no A&E and no scan.
Artificial tears were specifically advised to be obtained from the chemist for daytime use.
Doctor advised nothing for the previously reported borderline cholesterol.
Negative finding qualified as 'not really dizzy' rather than a definite no dizziness.
